summary: This preregistered, fully archived paired experiment tested whether a Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) intervention reduces deterministic-verifier-detected semantic violations on a 240-task synthetic NetOps bank using gpt-5-mini and a pybatfish-style validator. Execution and archived analysis are internally consistent: all 240 paired tasks produced verifier-compliant configurations in both arms (n11=240), no repairs were applied, and the paired estimate is 0.0 (exact McNemar p=1.00, 95% CI [0.0,0.0]). Strengths: preregistration, complete artifact archiving and hashing, deterministic reconciliation, and clear limitations disclosure. Main weaknesses: (a) a prespecified second primary comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and lacks a recorded rationale in the artifacts; (b) the preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one initial generation reused across arms) substantially reduced the test’s sensitivity to detect GVR benefits because both arms received the same candidate so repairs were never invoked; (c) these design choices materially limit the confirmatory claims that can be drawn about GVR’s effectiveness beyond the specific shared-generation setting.
critical_issues: A prespecified primary comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained baseline) reported in the preregistration was not executed; the run artifacts contain no recorded rationale for this omission. The manuscript must explicitly state this deviation, point to the exact artifact(s) showing the omission, and discuss its consequences for interpretation and the preregistered multiplicity plan.

The preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms) was chosen prior to execution and is recorded in the execution_contract; that design makes the paired comparison insensitive to per-condition stochastic variation and thus to typical GVR benefits. The manuscript must clearly and unambiguously state that: (a) this design choice was preregistered; (b) it caused repair never to be invoked because the shared candidate satisfied verifier predicates in all tasks; and (c) the confirmatory null result therefore pertains only to the shared-generation semantics rather than to independent-generation GVR pipelines.

The paper sometimes presents the study as a general confirmatory test of GVR; given (1) and (2) above, the manuscript must revise any wording that implies broader confirmatory validity (e.g., remove or qualify statements that read as general evidence that GVR does not help). All contribution claims must be precisely bounded to the archived experimental design and its recorded limitations.

The preregistration and Disclosure Statement indicate multiplicity handling (two prespecified primary comparisons with Bonferroni correction). Because only one of those comparisons was executed, the manuscript must state how multiplicity treatment was applied in practice (or why it was not applicable) and update the statistical-text accordingly. Point to the archived analysis artifacts that support the reported p-values/CIs.
required_revisions: Add a concise, prominent Methods/Preregistration subsection or table that (i) lists each prespecified primary and secondary comparison, (ii) indicates which were executed and which were not, and (iii) cites the exact archived artifact paths and SHA-256 entries that demonstrate execution or non-execution (resolvable from supplied artifacts).

Explicitly and unambiguously state that generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate was preregistered, explain in plain terms why that choice reduces sensitivity to GVR (replicate the artifact-backed causal chain: one model call → shared candidate → repair not invoked → no discordant pairs), and qualify all conclusions to reflect that limitation.

Correct any text that implies generalizable null evidence for GVR beyond the shared-generation setting. Replace broad-language claims with narrowly framed conclusions that are directly supported by the archived artifacts (e.g., "Under preregistered shared-generation semantics on this synthetic verifier-checked task bank, GVR produced no additional verifier-detected improvements").

Clarify how the preregistered multiplicity (two primary comparisons) was handled in analysis and reporting given the unexecuted comparison; either (a) report the decision rule used post-hoc supported by artifacts, or (b) state that multiplicity correction was preregistered but only one comparison was executed and therefore the correction was not applied—include artifact citations.

Include in the manuscript a short artifact-guided evidence-to-claim itemization (1–3 lines) tying each principal numeric claim (n11, model_call counts, repair_applied=false, p-value, CI) to the specific archived file/path and hash already present in the evidence bundle (resolvable from supplied artifacts).
optional_revisions: Briefly expand the Discussion’s recommendations with an explicit prioritized next-step plan (using only archival-executable options described in the preregistration) such as running independent per-condition generation, injecting adversarial/golden tasks that would trigger repairs, or evaluating multiple generator families; label these as future work and do not claim they were executed.

Condense provenance-heavy paragraphs and move machine-readable provenance pointers into a compact table or appendix-like paragraph (still within the five-page limit) so the narrative foregrounds scientific interpretation rather than metadata bookkeeping.

Add one small illustrative example (task id and the exact shared-initial response and validator trace) from the archived representative_tasks to make the result more concrete for readers; cite the artifact hash and path.
